description: In decoupled consensus/execution architectures or modular BFT systems, the component responsible for maintaining the ledger state must blindly trust the consensus oracle for finality updates. If the ledger component only verifies that a finalized block is part of the current canonical chain, it misses the temporal invariant of finality: finality is an append-only, irreversible state. A Byzantine actor or faulty consensus module can exploit this by sending a stale or malicious update that moves the finalized pointer backward, un-finalizing previously secured blocks and exposing the system to deep reorganizations and double-spend attacks.
trigger_condition: A consensus update message (e.g., fork choice update) is received where the newly specified finalized block is an ancestor of the currently finalized block.
test_template: 1. **Initialize:** Start a target node and sync a linear chain of blocks: `Genesis -> Block 1 -> Block 2 -> Block 3`.
